headline.purpose: Section titles, e.g. "Your week so far".

script.purpose: Ephesis — wordmark, day-of-week heading, morning greeting only. No fourth use.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: Default state of every card, block, and button.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover, drag, and current/next timeline block.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing for every transition; soft decelerating glide, no bounce or elastic.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Progress-ring fill, panel reveals, arrival float.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one main action per screen; rose fill, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 15.5px; font-weight: 600; color: #fff; background: var(--accent); border: none; border-radius: var(--r-md); padding: 14px 22px; min-height: 48px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: var(--shadow-rest); transition: background 160ms var(--ease), box-shadow 260ms var(--ease), transform 160ms var(--ease); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-strong); box-shadow: var(--shadow-lift); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Supporting action beside a primary button; blush fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--accent-strong); background: var(--surface-blush); border: none; border-radius: var(--r-md); padding: 13px 16px; min-height: 44px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 160ms var(--ease); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--surface-deep); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Dismissals and "later" paths; skipping is always quiet and guilt-free.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text-muted); background: none; border: none; padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: var(--r-md); cursor: pointer; min-height: 44px; transition: background 160ms var(--ease), color 160ms var(--ease); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface-blush); color: var(--text); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Timeline Block Card
components.description: Signature component: a flexible/protected timeline block at rest, height mapped to duration.
components.css: .ds-block { background: var(--surface); border-radius: var(--r-md); box-shadow: var(--shadow-rest); padding: 9px 13px; } .ds-block-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; } .ds-block-title { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 600; font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-block-time { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--text-muted); margin-top: 1px; }

components.name: Category Tag
components.description: Small pill in a category-specific rose/cream tint; every category gets equal visual dignity.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; padding: 2.5px 9px; border-radius: var(--r-pill); letter-spacing: 0.02em; background: #f6e8dc; color: #9a7350; } .ds-tag-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; }

components.name: Question Note
components.description: Signature component: the app's only "attention" voice — overlap nudge and boundary confirmation.
components.html: These two overlap — want me to nudge one?
components.css: .ds-note { background: #f7e3e7; border-radius: var(--r-md); padding: 12px 15px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 9px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-rest); } .ds-note-txt { font-size: 13px; color: #8f4f63; } .ds-note-btns { display: flex; gap: 9px; align-items: center; } .ds-note-btn { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; color: #8f4f63; background: rgba(255,255,255,.82); border: none; border-radius: var(--r-pill); padding: 8px 15px; min-height: 32px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 160ms var(--ease); } .ds-note-btn:hover { background: #fff; } .ds-note-btn-ghost { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: #b58a99; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 8px 6px; min-height: 32px; }

components.name: Progress Ring
components.description: Signature component: additive-only progress, petal-to-rose gradient fill, fills once on change.
components.css: .ds-ring { width: 92px; height: 92px; } .ds-ring circle { fill: none; stroke-width: 9; stroke-linecap: round; } .ds-ring-track { stroke: var(--surface-blush); } .ds-ring-fill { stroke: url(#ds-rose-grad); transform: rotate(-90deg); transform-origin: 50% 50%; transition: stroke-dashoffset 420ms var(--ease); } .ds-ring-text { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 600; font-size: 19px; fill: var(--text); }

narrative.northStar: The Gentle Morning in a Porcelain Room
narrative.overview:
Soft Start lives in a warm, unhurried material world: a porcelain-toned room where nothing casts a hard shadow, and one rose-lit morning moment a day is allowed to glow. The palette is a single rose-and-cream family stretched across almost the whole interface — porcelain and white for the room itself, blush tints for anything nested inside it, and a warm rose-brown ink instead of black. The only saturated departures are deliberate and narrow: sage means done and nothing else, apricot means the app has a gentle question and nothing else, and a soft rose gradient field is reserved for the single arrival moment each morning. Everything else stays quiet by design — this is a system for someone who is already disciplined and just needs the negotiation removed, so the interface never argues, alarms, or scores.

Depth comes entirely from tinted shadow blooms and blush-tint layering, never from borders or outlines — corners are generous everywhere and hairlines appear only inside tables and dividers. Motion is calm and singular: one orchestrated moment per screen (the arrival's rose-field fade and float-dock, the progress ring's fill, the once-a-day petal drift), plus quiet hover/press micro-interactions, with every transition collapsing to near-instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

Confirmed rejections: no red anywhere, no borders for depth, no badges or streak-shaming, no countdown or urgency language, no gamification currency, no comparison of today's plan against an "original." A day begun late is optimized, never mourned — the visual system's calmness is a direct expression of that product stance, not decoration on top of it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm porcelain and white rooms; rose-brown ink instead of black
Depth via rose-tinted shadow blooms + blush-tint nesting — never borders, never shadow-on-shadow
Ephesis script reserved for exactly three moments: wordmark, day-of-week heading, morning greeting
Sage = done, apricot = gentle question, deep blush = the question's field — each color has exactly one job
One orchestrated motion moment per screen; everything eases out, nothing bounces or loops

rules.name: The No-Red Rule
rules.body: Red never appears anywhere in the product. Apricot carries all "gentle attention" duty; sage carries all "completion" duty. Neither ever borrows the other's job.

rules.name: The Deep-Blush Question Rule
rules.body: The #F7E3E7 field / #8F4F63 text pairing renders only when the app is gently asking the user something — the overlap nudge, the boundary-crossing confirmation. It never appears as decoration or as a third "info" color.

rules.name: The Equal-Dignity Rule
rules.body: All seven block categories render in matched-saturation members of the same rose+cream family. No category reads as more important than another.

rules.name: The Three-Places Rule
rules.body: Ephesis script renders in exactly three places — the wordmark, the day-of-week heading, and the morning greeting. Never a fourth.

rules.name: The Tint-Not-Stack Rule
rules.body: Nested cards and chips gain depth from a blush background fill, never from a second layer of shadow.

dos: Do derive every color, size, radius, and duration from the tokens above.
Do add whitespace before reaching for a divider, and a divider before ever reaching for a border.
Do give every empty state (blank weekend, fully-rested day) an inviting, additive message plus a one-tap way to add something.
Do keep one primary button and one signature motion moment per screen.
Do write button labels as concrete verbs and outcomes in sentence case ("Save changes", not "Submit").
donts: Don't use red, exclamation marks, or countdowns anywhere — the single approved exception is "Wow! What a day." on a 100%-complete evening, which fires at most once per day.
Don't show negative counts ("3 missed", "2 overdue") — always reframe as progress made, never as a deficit.
Don't stack shadows on nested surfaces — nest with a blush tint instead.
Don't let apricot or deep-blush drift into decorative use; both are reserved entirely for the app's gentle-question moments.
Don't render Ephesis script anywhere outside the wordmark, the day-of-week heading, and the morning greeting.
Don't animate more than one orchestrated moment per screen, and always provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
